files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.ListContractsResponse
files.Summary:
Response of ListarContratos (servicos/contrato) — the page of Service Contracts registered in Omie. A contract is a price registry: it holds the negotiated value and the validity period agreed with one client, and must never be billed through.

The listing exists so callers can resolve a contract by the number the user knows (cNumCtr) without asking Omie one call per contract: Omie exposes no search by contract number, and repeated single consults are what trips its "Consumo redundante" gate. List once, index in memory — the same approach as the service catalog.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.ListContractsServiceItem
files.Summary: One service line of a contract in the listing.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.ListContractsServiceItemHeader

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.ListServiceRegistrationResponse
files.Summary: Response of ListarCadastroServico (servicos/servico) — paged list of registered services. Used to resolve a service's unit price/description by its nCodServ. The servicos/servico endpoint pages with the n-prefixed keys (nPagina/nTotPaginas/nRegistros/nTotRegistros), not the generic pagina/total_de_paginas.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.OmieCategory
files.Summary: A usable account of the Omie chart of accounts (ListarCategorias).

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.OmieCheckingAccount
files.Summary: A usable checking account of Omie (ListarContasCorrentes).

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.OmieContractInfo
files.Summary: A Service Contract of Omie as callers consume it: the number the user knows, the validity period and the negotiated value, with the dates already parsed. Projected from the listing so no caller has to deal with Omie's dd/MM/yyyy strings or with which key carries what.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.OmieInvoiceRpsStatus
files.Summary: RPS and batch status codes in Omie (cStatusRps / cStatusLote), as documented by the API. Both fields use the same three digits.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.OmieServiceDetail
files.Summary: The full registration of a service (ConsultarCadastroServico). The listing does not carry these fields and including a service order requires them on every item: LC 116 service code, municipal service code and tax classification. None of them can be invented — when they are missing from the Omie registration, the caller should stop and say which service to fix.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.OmieServiceInfo
files.Summary:
A service of the Omie catalog, as ListarCadastroServico returns it.

The two codes exist and are not interchangeable: is the business code (cCodigo, e.g. "SRV00016"), the one applications store in their own configuration, while is Omie's internal identifier (nCodServico), the only one accepted when building service order items. Translating one into the other is the reason the whole catalog is read.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.OmieServiceInvoiceStatus
files.Summary: The service invoice (NFS-e) of a service order and the progress of the RPS it came from. Issuing is a process, not an instant: Omie transmits the RPS and the city hall authorizes it later, so there is a window in which the invoice exists as a request and has no number yet.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DTOs.Responses.OmieServiceOrderStatus
files.Summary: Fiscal state of a service order in Omie, as StatusOS returns it: which stage it sits in, whether it was cancelled, whether it was already invoiced and — when it was — the NFS-e that came out of it.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.DependencyInjection
files.Summary: Extensions to register the Omie API client in the DI container.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Json.OmieFlexibleStringConverter
files.Summary: Reads as text a field Omie may send as text or as a number. Status codes and the NFS-e number are documented as string, but arrive sometimes as "0" and sometimes as 0 depending on the call — and a here would bring down the whole response read over one field's formatting.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.OmieFaultClassifier
files.Summary:
Classifies Omie failure messages so callers can react programmatically (e.g. switch an OS create to an update when the integration code already exists) instead of string-matching Omie text themselves. This component surfaces faults as failed (it deliberately does not throw — see the comment on OmieApiClient._staticClient), so the markers live here in one place.

VERIFY (Omie test app): confirm the exact faultstring wording for the duplicate-integration-code and not-found cases against the current Omie responses and adjust the markers below if needed.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.OmieOrderStage
files.Summary: The service order stage (cEtapa) in Omie. The API documents five values — 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 (invoice) — but an account may have its own Kanban columns, and the query returns the real stage (60 has been seen). Echoing that stage back on a change means sending a value outside the domain the API accepts; since cEtapa is optional on AlterarOS, the right move is to omit it and leave the order where it is.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieCategoryProvider
files.Summary:
Resolves the category (cCodCateg) a service order carries in Omie. Omie requires the category on inclusion and every account has its own chart of accounts — which is why it is discovered in the registration instead of hardcoded: the categories are listed and the first of the configured preferences is picked by name.

Only accounts that can take a revenue entry are considered: conta_receita = "S", active, not a totalizer (totalizers are just groupings of the chart of accounts) and not a transfer account. Filtering by name alone could land on an expense account with a similar name.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieCheckingAccountProvider
files.Summary:
Omie checking accounts (geral/contacorrente/) — the list an application offers so the user can pick where the receivable of a service order lands (nCodCC, required on inclusion).

Blocked accounts are left out: Omie lists them but does not accept entries on them.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieClientDirectoryProvider
files.Summary:
Omie client registration indexed by document (CNPJ/CPF) — the way to discover the client code (codigo_cliente_omie), and the only one: Omie does not look a client up by document, and the typed client (IOmieApiClient) only consults by the very code one is trying to discover. The whole registration is listed (ListarClientes, paginated) and searched by document.

The document is compared by digits only: in Omie it usually comes formatted ("12.345.678/0001-99") while applications tend to store it clean — comparing as text would find nobody.

The listing is expensive, so it is cached for . A client just registered in Omie may, for that long, still not be found.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieContractProvider
files.Summary:
Omie Service Contracts, read whole (ListarContratos, paginated) and indexed by the contract number (cNumCtr) — the number a caller's own configuration stores, because it is what the user reads in Omie. A contract is a price registry: it carries the negotiated value and the validity period of one client, and is never billed through.

Listed whole and cached for , never consulted one by one. A screen that shows contracts in a grid would otherwise ask Omie once per row, and Omie answers a burst of repeated calls with "Consumo redundante detectado" — which blocks the app_key for every other integration, not just the grid.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieDirectApiClient
files.Summary:
Raw call to the Omie API, for the registrations does not cover or covers without the fields a caller needs. It concentrates three details that any new call would otherwise repeat:

  1. the Content-Type goes without the charset parameter — with it, the Omie gateway answers a SOAP "Bad Request" envelope (and that is exactly what PostAsJsonAsync/JsonContent would send);
  2. business errors come in the body (faultstring) alongside an HTTP 5xx — without reading it, the failure turns into an "InternalServerError" that says nothing;
  3. consumption refusals (REDUNDANT, MISUSE_API_PROCESS) are not request errors and get their own treatment (see ).

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieServiceCatalogProvider
files.Summary:
Omie service catalog, read whole (ListarCadastroServico, paginated) and indexed by the business code (cCodigo) — the code applications store in their own configuration. This is how the nCodServico, the description and the unit price of a service are discovered: Omie exposes no search by cCodigo, so the catalog is listed and searched in memory.

The result is cached for because Omie refuses repeated ListarCadastroServico calls in a short window ("Consumo redundante detectado") — without the cache, opening a screen and generating a service order right after would drop the second call.

files.Title: NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieServiceOrderBillingProvider
files.Summary:
Invoicing of a single service order in Omie — the documented path to issue the NFS-e of one OS, which does not cover and therefore goes through the direct client:

  1. StatusOS (servicos/os/): fiscal state of the order — stage, whether it was cancelled, whether it was already invoiced and the NFS-e that came out of it. It is the query that says whether there is anything to do, and the one that confirms the result afterwards.
  2. ValidarOS (servicos/osp/): Omie's validation before invoicing. It is what points out, in the API's own words, which required data is missing on the order or on the client registration — instead of finding out through the city hall's rejection, after the invoice was already requested.
  3. FaturarOS (servicos/osp/): invoices that order. The equivalent of "Faturar Selecionada" in the Omie UI — not to be confused with FaturarLoteOS (servicos/oslote/), which invoices every order of a stage and, triggered for one client, would take the others along.

None of them invents data: the invoice content is the order's. What is decided here is only when to ask for the invoice.
